item.content:encoded:
from: How Cerebras Deploys Trillion-Parameter AI Models

One of the most frequently asked questions we get is how we deploy large models on Cerebras wafer-scale chips. A single Cerebras WSE-3T wafer has 44 GB of on-chip memory, and trillion-parameter frontier models need terabytes for their weights alone.

单个 Cerebras WSE-3T 晶圆拥有 44 GB 的片上内存，而万亿参数的前沿模型 terabytes 仅用于其权重。

In this post, we’ll explain how we split a large frontier model across multiple WSE-3T wafers, to run multi-trillion parameter models at 1000-2000+ tokens per second.

在本文中，我们将解释如何将大规模前沿模型分割到多个 WSE-3T 晶圆上，以每秒 1000-2000+ tokens 的速度运行万亿参数模型。

We’ll use the open source model Kimi K3, with ~3 trillion parameters, as an illustrative example.

我们将使用开源模型 Kimi K3，作为具有 ~3万亿参数 的说明性示例。

By the end, you’ll understand:

最终，你将会理解：

  • How we fit the full model into on-chip memory
  • How we map the model across multiple chips
  • How we handle a high # of concurrent requests
  • 如何将完整模型适配至片上存储器
  • 如何将模型映射至多个芯片
  • 如何处理高并发请求

Breaking it down with Kimi K3

与Kimi K3一起拆解

Kimi K3 is an open source, 3T parameter model with 69 linear-attention layers and 24 dense layers.

Kimi K3 是一个开源的 3T 参数模型，包含 69 层线性注意力层和 24 层稠密层。

It scores an impressive 88.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (vs. GPT-5.6 Sol’s 88.8%) and 91.2% on BrowseComp (vs. GPT-5.6 Sol’s 90.4%). These results demonstrate frontier-level coding and agentic capabilities, even outperforming leading proprietary models on some benchmarks. Read more about Kimi K3 here.

它在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上取得了令人瞩目的 88.3% 的成绩（对比 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 88.8%），并在 BrowseComp 上取得了 91.2% 的成绩（对比 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 90.4%）。这些结果展现了前沿级别的编码和智能体能力，甚至在某些基准测试中超越了领先的专有模型。点击此处阅读有关 Kimi K3 的更多内容。

For this illustrative example, we use:

对于这个示例，我们使用了以下内容：

  • A 256k assumed average request size
  • 4-bit weight quantization (like the Hugging Face implementation)
  • An 8-bit KV cache
  • 假设平均请求大小为 256k
  • 4-bit 权重量化（如 Hugging Face 实现）
  • 8-bit KV 缓存

#1: Size of Each layer

#1：各层的大小

To calculate the total number of Cerebras WSE-3T wafers we need to support Kimi K3, let’s first calculate the size of each model layer.

要计算支持 Kimi K3 所需的 Cerebras WSE-3T 晶圆总数，我们先计算每个模型层的大小。

Kimi K3 has 3 trillion parameters. If all 3T parameters are stored at 4 bits each, the raw parameter payload is:

Kimi K3 的参数规模为 3 万亿。若以 4 位（bit）精度存储每个参数，其原始参数负载的计算方式如下：

  • 参数总量：3 × 10¹²
  • 每个参数占用：4 位

将位转换为字节（1 字节 = 8 位），可得：

3 × 10¹² × 4 ÷ 8 = 1.5 × 10¹² 字节，即 1.5 TB。

Dividing that payload by 93 layers then gives:

将该有效负载除以 93 层后得到：

#2: Number of Wafers

#2：晶圆数量

Now that we know each layer needs about 16 GB, we can figure out how many layers fit on each 44 GB wafer. The answer depends on the layer type:

现在我们知道每层大约需要 16 GB，我们就可以计算出每块 44 GB 的 wafer 能容纳多少层。答案取决于层类型：

  • Dense layers need additional room for a KV cache, because each dense (full-attention) layer stores the keys and values for every token in every active request. So, we place one dense layer per wafer and leave the remaining SRAM for its KV cache.
  • Linear-attention layers do not require additional room for a KV cache. Instead of storing keys and values for every token, a linear-attention layer keeps a small, fixed-size state per request, regardless of context length. That leaves room for two linear layers per wafer (2 × 16 GB = 32 GB).
  • 密集层需要额外的空间来存放KV缓存，因为每个密集层都会存储所有活跃请求中每个token的键和值（即全注意力机制）。因此，我们在每片晶圆上放置一个密集层，并将剩余的SRAM用于KV缓存。
  • 线性注意力层则不需要额外的KV缓存空间。不同于存储每个token的键和值，线性注意力层仅保留每个请求的固定大小的状态，与上下文长度无关。这使得每片晶圆上可以放置两个线性层（2 × 16 GB = 32 GB）。

Therefore, with Kimi K3’s 69 linear layers and 24 dense layers, we get:

因此，基于 Kimi K3 的 69 linear layers and 24 dense layers，我们得到：

This gives us a total wafer count of 35 + 24 = 59 wafers.

这让我们得到总晶圆数：35 + 24 = 59 晶圆。

#3: Connecting the wafers together

#3: 将晶圆连接在一起

Cerebras executes models in a pipeline. After the Cerebras compiler maps the model layers across regions of wafers, the runtime maps the path for tokens to flow between wafers. For ultrafast latency, only activations need to be passed between the wafers, and this can be done via RDMA over Ethernet. This is roughly 2 microseconds per hop.

Cerebras 执行模型在流水线中。之后 Cerebras 编译器映射模型层跨硅片区域，运行时 tokens 在硅片之间的流动路径。为了实现超低延迟，只有激活需要在硅片之间传输，并可通过 RDMA over Ethernet 实现。大约 2 microseconds 每个跳。

It’s important to emphasize that because each Cerebras wafer has 44 GB of on-chip SRAM and each layer is only 16 GB, we are typically able to fit entire layers of the model directly on the chip.

重要的是要强调，因为每个 Cerebras 晶圆有 44 GB 的片上 SRAM，且每一层仅为 16 GB，我们通常能够容纳整个 model 的层直接在芯片上。

This means that in most cases, the model weights never have to move, and layers don’t need to be split across wafers. Only activations cross from one wafer to the next.

这意味着在大多数情况下，模型权重无需移动，层也不需要跨芯片分布。只有激活值会在芯片之间传输。

#4: How we serve 1 request

#4: 我们如何服务单个请求

Now that we have our wafers connected together and the model laid out, we can think of each wafer as one stage in an assembly line: the model’s weights for each stage stay in place, and the request’s intermediate results move through the layer stages.

现在我们已经将这些晶圆连接在一起，并且把模型完成了布局，我们可以把每个晶圆看作一条装配线的 一个阶段：每个阶段的模型权重保持不变，请求的中间结果会穿过各层阶段。

For example, Wafer 1 runs model layers 1–2 and sends its activations to wafer 2. Wafer 2 runs layers 3–4 and passes its results to Wafer 3, and so on until the last wafer produces the next token.

例如，Wafer 1 运行模型层 1–2，并将它的激活传递给 Wafer 2。Wafer 2 运行层 3–4，并将结果传递给 Wafer 3，以此类推，直到最后一个 Wafer 生成下一个 Token。

#5: How we serve many requests

#5：我们如何处理大量请求

This raises a common misconception. If a token has to travel through each wafer in order, doesn’t each wafer sit idle while it waits for its turn? In effect, wouldn’t the system be running at a batch size of one?

这提出了一个常见的误区。如果 token 必须按顺序通过每一片 wafer，那么每一片 wafer 在等待轮次时难道都会空闲吗？换言之，系统难道不是以批量大小为 one 运行吗？

No! If we only sent one request down the line at a time and waited for it to complete before starting the next request, this would be an inefficient use of the pipeline. Instead, we keep the entire pipeline full with different requests. Because the model is split into pipeline stages already, each stage can work on a different request at the same time.

不！如果我们一次只在流水线中发送一个请求，并在启动下一个请求前等待它完成，这将是对流水线的低效利用。相反，我们用不同的请求保持整个流水线处于满载状态。因为模型已经被拆分为流水线阶段，所以每个阶段可以同时处理不同的请求。

While stage 3 processes a token for request A, stage 2 processes one for request B, and stage 1 one for request C. In our example, each stage is a layer. In production, Cerebras uses much finer-grained stages, and many more of them.

当 stage 3 正在为请求 A 处理 Token 时，stage 2 正在为请求 B 处理一个 Token，stage 1 正在为请求 C 处理一个 Token。在本示例中，每个 stage 都是一个层。在生产环境中，Cerebras 使用更细粒度的 stage，且数量更多。

Loading player…

正在加载播放器…

Each stage can also process a micro-batch, a small group of requests, rather than a single request. So the number of requests in flight is roughly the number of stages times the micro-batch size.

每个阶段也可以处理一个 微批次 (micro-batch)，即一小组请求，而不是单个请求。因此，正在处理中的请求数量大致是阶段数量乘以微批次大小。

Loading player…

加载玩家中…玩家加载中…

To understand the tradeoff, smaller micro-batches make each request even faster, while larger micro-batches increase total throughput.

要理解这种权衡，更小的 micro-batches 会使每个请求更快，而更大的 micro-batches 会提高总吞吐量。

#6: How many requests can we serve?

#6: 我们能服务多少请求？

The amount of on-chip memory allocated to KV cache determines the maximum number of concurrent requests. Every request in flight needs its own KV cache on each dense-layer wafer, so the size of on-chip memory sets the ceiling on concurrent requests. As explained above, we only need to calculate KV cache requirements for dense layers.

分配给 KV cache 的片上内存大小决定了最大并发请求数。每个进行中的请求在每个密集层晶圆上都需要自己专属的 KV cache，因此片上内存的大小设定了并发请求的上限。正如上文所述，我们只需要计算密集层对 KV cache 的需求。

For each 44 GB wafer that already has one dense layer, we can calculate the remaining space for the KV cache with:

对于每个容量为 44 GB 的晶圆，如果其已经包含一层密集结构，我们可以通过以下方法计算剩余的 KV 缓存空间：

Total wafer storage - size of one dense layer. In this case:

总晶圆储存 - 一个密集层的尺寸。在这种情况下：

Calculating the # of Concurrent Requests

计算并发请求数量

To find the number of concurrent requests supported for any particular model mapping, we first calculate how much cache a single 256k request takes up:

要找出任何特定模型映射支持多少并发请求，我们首先计算单个 256k 请求占用多少缓存：

To then calculate the total number of concurrent requests this configuration would support, we divide:

然后，为了计算此配置所能支持的并发请求总数，我们除以：

The total number of concurrent requests represents the number of simultaneous requests moving through the pipeline at any point in time. Unlike a GPU batch, those requests don’t wait for one another to finish, they stream through the pipeline continuously.

并发请求总数表示在任意时间点同时流经流水线的请求数量。与 GPU 批处理不同，这些请求不会相互等待完成，而是持续不断地流经流水线。

Of course, neither concurrency nor batch size tells you exactly how efficiently an inference system performs. When evaluating the throughput of an inference system, the more meaningful metric is total token throughput per unit of power (e.g. tokens per second per megawatt), when measured at the same output generation speed.

当然，并发和批大小都不能精确告诉你一个推理系统执行效率如何。在评估推理系统的吞吐量时，更有意义的指标是总 token 吞吐量，单位为每单位功率（例如 token/秒每兆瓦），且应在相同的输出生成速度下进行测量。

How this scales beyond 3T parameters

这 如何 在 3T 参数之外 扩展

将语言模型扩展到 3T 参数会带来 记忆管理、训练效率和推理延迟的独特挑战。最近 在 sparse attention 和 model parallelism 方面的进展展示了有前景的结果，但 compute cost 和 model quality 之间的权衡仍然是 关键 研究 重点。

The same approach extends to larger models: calculate the memory needed for weights and request state, distribute the model across wafers, and connect them into a pipeline. Each additional wafer contributes compute and on-chip memory, allowing us to accommodate models that exceed the capacity of any single chip.

同样的方法也适用于更大的模型：计算权重和请求状态所需的内存，将模型分布在多个晶圆上，并将其连接成一个流水线。每增加一个晶圆都会贡献计算能力和片上内存，使我们能够容纳超出任何单一芯片容量的模型。

from: AI and the Fall? of the Creative Class

America is Losing Hundreds of Thousands of Jobs in Media, Film & the Arts. How Much is AI to Blame?

美国媒体、电影和艺术领域损失了数十万个工作岗位。AI 究竟负多少责任？

Thanks for reading! If you haven’t subscribed, please click the button below:

感谢阅读！如果您还没有订阅，请点击下面的按钮：

By subscribing, you’ll join over 80,000 people who read Apricitas!

通过订阅，您将成为超过 80,000 名阅读 Apricitas 的读者之一！

America has lost more than 200k jobs in “creative” industries over the last four years, with roughly 50k lost within the last year alone. That makes for one of the worst stretches for media employment in modern US history, with similar job loss intensity and duration occurring only during the major economic recessions of 2001 and 2008. Yet there’s no generalized recession today—instead, this period of job loss coincides with the rise of AI systems that can compose wholesale novels, photorealistic images, soundalike music, and practically every other form of digital art, en masse and at extremely low costs. Is this the fall of the Creative Class?

美国在过去四年中，创意产业失去了超过20万个工作岗位，仅在过去一年就失去了大约5万个。这使得这成为现代美国历史上媒体就业的最糟糕时期之一，类似的失业强度和持续时间仅在2001年和2008年的重大经济衰退期间出现。然而，今天并没有大规模的经济衰退——相反，这一失业时期与能够创作整本小说、照片级真实的图像、听起来像音乐的声音以及几乎所有其他形式的数字艺术的AI系统的兴起同时发生。这是创意阶层的衰落吗？

Proving the exact amount of AI-driven job loss in the arts is extremely difficult. Media firms are decidedly coy about their AI use, both to protect against public backlash and, more financially important, to preserve the legal basis for their copyrights. The effects of AI are also hard to disentangle from other factors currently affecting arts businesses, like consolidation in Hollywood, offshoring of content production, or the continued displacement of traditional media providers in favor of social media creators. Yet perhaps the clearest evidence of AI’s influence is just that all subsectors of the digital arts industry are losing jobs, while in-person entertainment is still growing at a healthy pace.

证明艺术领域 AI 驱动的岗位流失的确切数量极其困难。媒体公司对其 AI 使用极为谨慎，既是为了规避公众反弹，更是为了保护其版权的法律基础。AI 的影响同样难以从目前影响艺术业务的其他因素中剥离，如 Hollywood 的整合、内容制作的外包，或传统媒体提供商被社交媒体创作者取代的持续趋势。然而，或许 AI 的影响力最明确的证据就是所有数字艺术子行业都在流失岗位，而现场娱乐仍以健康的速度增长。

Some of those digital job losses are just a continuation of prior trends, like in the publishing industry where technological change has been continually grinding away newspaper and magazine jobs for decades. Yet for sectors like live broadcasting, streaming, or graphic design, recent experience is an unusual downturn compared to the tranquility of years prior. Then there’s the worst-hit sector, movie & sound recording, which has been bleeding jobs at a nearly unprecedented pace over the last three years.

其中一些数字化就业损失只是延续了以往的趋势，例如在出版行业，技术变革几十年来持续削减着报纸和杂志的工作岗位。然而，对于现场广播、流媒体或图形设计等行业而言，最近的衰退与过去几年的稳定时期相比显得异常。从最受影响的电影和录音制作行业来看，在过去三年中，几乎以前所未有的速度流失着工作岗位。

Hollywood has never seen a stretch as bad as the last four years, with the movie & TV industry losing more than 100k jobs, nearly one-third of the sector’s total. At the depths touched this summer, total employment was lower than at any point since the 2008 recession and approaching the lowest point in 30 years. The streaming era has proven an extremely difficult transition, with traditional films and TV shows losing watch time to user-generated and increasingly AI-assisted or AI-generated content flows.

好莱坞过去四年所经历的衰退前所未有，其电影和电视产业损失了超过10万个就业岗位，几乎占到该行业总就业人数的三分之一。在今年夏天的低点，总就业人数低于2008年金融危机以来的最低点，并逼近近30年来的最低水平。流媒体时代的转型证明极其艰难，传统电影和电视节目在观看时间上逐渐让位于用户生成内容，以及日益依赖人工智能辅助或由人工智能生成的内容流。

Overall, nearly half the media job losses of the last four years have been concentrated in the movie & sound recording sector that includes Hollywood. Written publishing has been the next-largest source of job loss, with employment down by more than 70k over the same time frame. Yet the job losses have by no means been contained to any particular part of media; instead they’ve hit nearly every subsector at some point. Nor do they show any sign of abating, with losses consistently hovering at around 50k per year and even accelerating in recent months. Will further AI development continue displacing workers in creative industries?

总体而言，过去四年里近一半的媒体职位裁员集中在电影和音频录制行业（ Hollywood）。书面出版是接下来最大的裁员来源，在此期间就业下降超过 70k。然而，这些裁员并未局限于媒体的任何特定部分；相反，它们在某个时点影响了几乎所有子行业。而且，裁员态势似乎没有减缓，损失每年保持在约 50k，甚至在最近几个月加速了。进一步的 AI 发展将继续导致创意行业的工人被替代吗？

Can the Arts Business Model Survive?

艺术产业的商业模式能够生存下去吗？

To understand what could happen to the business of art amidst the rise of AI, it’s important to understand what did happen to it during the first digital transition, the rise of the internet.

要理解在 AI 兴起之际艺术商业可能会发生什么，了解在第一次数字化转型——即互联网的兴起——期间它确实发生了什么，这一点至关重要。

It was the turn of the millennium, and Metallica had a problem. Demos of their upcoming, unreleased tracks were bouncing around radio and the internet, originally leaked onto a new internet file-sharing website called Napster. There they found thousands of files shared amongst hundreds of thousands of users, many of which were direct rips of albums that sold for $15 being offered for free. The most anticipated albums were often leaked online even before they were on store shelves. Metallica sued Napster for copyright infringement, and they were soon joined by separate suits from other prominent artists and eventually the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).

那是在千禧年交替之际，Metallica 遇到了一个难题。他们即将发行但尚未正式发布的曲目小样在广播和互联网上广泛传播，最初是泄露到了一个名为 Napster 的新型互联网文件共享网站上。在那里，成千上万个文件在数十万用户之间共享，其中许多是直接盗录的、售价 $15 的专辑，却被免费提供。最受期待的专辑甚至在上架销售之前就经常在网上泄露。Metallica 因版权侵权起诉了 Napster，随后其他知名艺术家也纷纷提起单独诉讼，最终美国唱片业协会 (RIAA) 也加入了起诉。

Much of the general public was understandably unsympathetic to Metallica, perceived as a bunch of already-successful millionaires trying to bilk even more money from listeners, and were even less sympathetic towards the RIAA, perceived as scurrilous middlemen who take from artists and fans alike. But the two of them easily won their lawsuit, forcing Napster into bankruptcy. Yet Metallica may have been right on the law but were on the wrong side of technology; the RIAA had won the battle but was losing the war.

相当多的普通公众出于可以理解的理由对 Metallica 缺乏同情，他们被视为一群已经成功的百万富翁，试图从听众身上榨取更多金钱；而且他们对 RIAA 的同情程度甚至更低，后者被视为专横且可鄙的中介，同样从艺术家和粉丝那里拿走钱。但他们俩轻松赢得了诉讼，迫使 Napster 进入破产。然而 Metallica 可能在法律上是正确的，但他们在技术的错误一边；RIAA 赢了这场战斗，但正在失去战争。

The modern internet made file-sharing extremely easy, and no matter how much whac-a-mole companies played, they could not possibly catch every illegal upload. The perennial threat of piracy undermined their copyright and limited their ability to charge for music. Eventually, the value of individual songs fell to the point that companies like Spotify and Apple Music could swoop in to acquire massive catalogues, consolidate them, and charge a comparatively trivial fee for access. For what a single Metallica album would have cost in 2000, you can now get a month’s worth of unlimited access to nearly all human-made music.

现代互联网使文件共享变得极其容易，无论公司如何玩“打地鼠”游戏，都不可能抓住每一个非法上传者。长期存在的盗版威胁动摇了他们的版权根基，并限制了他们对音乐收费的能力。最终，单曲的价值跌落至谷底，Spotify 和 Apple Music 等公司得以乘虚而入，收购庞大的曲库，整合资源，并以相对微不足道的费用提供访问权限。用 2000 年购买一张 Metallica 专辑的钱，现在可以买到一个月近乎所有人类创作音乐的无限畅听权。

The music industry has never returned to the heyday paydays of the peak CD era—even without adjusting for inflation, streaming revenue pales in comparison to ‘90s physical media sales. This was a massive boon to consumers, but it was also a squeeze on musicians that forced them to fundamentally change their business model over time. Instead of just selling records to earn money directly, music itself increasingly became a loss-leading advertisement for the live concerts (and merch) that provided a growing share of artists’ income. Tours got longer, venues got bigger, ticket prices skyrocketed, and musicians frequently took on roles closer to public influencers than isolated artistes. Were it not for rising concert sales, the business model of music would have completely collapsed, and the income going to musicians would have cratered.

音乐产业从未回归过 CD 时代巅峰时的高峰收益， streaming revenue 也远不及 ’90s physical media sales。 这对消费者是巨大的福利，但对音乐人来说却是一股挤压力，迫使他们不得不随时间根本改变商业模式。 除了直接销售唱片赚钱，音乐本身越来越成为 loss-leading advertisement for live concerts (and merch) that provided a growing share of artists’ income。 巡演变长，场馆变大，票价飙升，音乐人经常扮演角色更接近 public influencers 而非 isolated artistes。 如果不是因为巡演销量的上升，音乐产业的商业模式本应完全崩溃，音乐人获得的收入也将暴跌。

Of course, there were still significant downsides to the transition into the streaming era. Bands (especially smaller ones) complain about the unending pressure to always be on tour. Musicians whose content was suited to home listening lost out to those more suited to giant festivals. Even accounting for concert revenues, musicians made less money than before. Yet musicians fared better than many areas of entertainment subsectors because there was a live component to fall back on—for many media industries, the digital era left no such comfort.

当然，转向流媒体时代仍然带来了显著的弊端。特别是小型乐队，他们抱怨始终处于巡演的不断压力之中。那些适合家庭聆听的内容的音乐家，输给了更适合大型音乐节的音乐家。即便算上演唱会收入，音乐家的收入也低于以前。然而，音乐家比娱乐产业的许多细分领域过得好，因为现场表演是他们可以依靠的组成部分——对于许多媒体产业来说，数字时代没有这样的慰藉。

Over time, the business of video has moved in the opposite direction of music—out of the theatre and into the home. Hollywood formerly made most of its money enticing customers to visit sold-out movie theatres, but these were gradually supplanted by broadcast TV, cable, and physical media. Yet because each successful technological leap increased total video watch time, the industry was still able to thrive amidst technological upheaval. That is, until the modern streaming era.

随着时间的推移，视频业务的发展方向与音乐行业完全相反：从电影院走向家庭。好莱坞过去靠吸引顾客来观看电影院的场次获利丰厚，但逐渐被广播电视、有线电视和实体媒体所取代。然而，每次成功的技术革新都增加了人们观看视频的总时长，因此整个行业仍然能够在技术变革中蓬勃发展。直到现代流媒体时代的到来，一切都发生了改变。

Today, the plethora of video options and the rise of social media have sent video producers into a vicious competition for limited attention. Even before adjusting for inflation, movie ticket sales ended last year down 25% from their 2019 peak, cable revenue is down 18% from its peak, and streaming revenue has not been able to compensate for the drop. The mountain of free user-generated content on YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, or social media was already presenting harsh competition for traditional video companies in the years before ChatGPT’s launch, and now streaming services are also competing with a flood of AI-generated content. The business model of video media is fundamentally getting squeezed, and unlike in the music industry, there’s basically no equivalent to live concerts that Hollywood can be used to ease the pain.

如今，视频选项的泛滥与社交媒体的崛起，让视频制作陷入了对有限注意力的恶性竞争。即使不考虑通货膨胀因素，去年电影票房收入较 2019 年峰值下降 25%，有线电视收入较峰值下降 18%，而流媒体收入无法弥补这一跌幅。在 ChatGPT 发布前几年，YouTube、Twitch、TikTok 等平台上海量的免费用户生成内容（UGC）已给传统视频公司带来严酷挑战，而现在流媒体服务还要面对 AI 生成内容的洪流冲击。视频媒体的商业模式从根本上正被挤压，与音乐行业不同，好莱坞基本没有类似现场演唱会的替代业务来缓解这种痛苦。

The actual worst-case scenario for creative workers amidst the AI revolution is something similar to what happened to the publishing industry after the advent of the internet—that is, near-total collapse of their fundamental business model. Newspapers used to employ roughly half a million people in the US, more than the entire oil industry, and now their payrolls are down nearly 85% and still dropping. Magazine publishers likewise have let 66% of their staff go since the 90s, while book publishers have lost 40%.

AI 革命对创意行业从业者而言的实际最坏情况，类似于互联网诞生后出版业遭遇的境况——即他们根本商业模式的几乎全面崩溃。在美国，过去报纸行业雇佣约有半百万人，这超过了整个石油行业的规模；而如今他们的人员支出已下降近 85%，且仍在持续下降。杂志出版商则自 90 年代以来裁撤了 66% 的员工，书籍出版商则损失了 40%。

The routine informational updates that previously formed newspapers’ bread-and-butter were all de-bundled—box scores moved to sports websites, stock movements went to financial websites, forecasts went to weather websites—each loss compounding on itself to undermine consumers’ need to buy the paper. Search engines became the first place people looked to for information, and newspapers’ advertising revenue rapidly started flowing to companies like Google instead. The collective of social media users became faster at breaking any news story than a daily paper could ever hope to be. When papers eventually did start aggressively paywalling content, the internet made it trivially easy for people to just copy the articles’ content and share it beyond the paywall. The entire business model had collapsed, to the point that now only a select few major newspapers can even survive.

过去构成报纸核心业务的常规资讯更新被全面拆分——球赛比分转移到了体育网站，股市行情流向了财经网站，天气预报归属气象网站——每一项流失相互叠加，共同动摇了读者购买报纸的必要性。搜索引擎成为人们获取信息的首选入口，报纸的广告收入迅速转流向 Google 等公司。社交媒体用户群体在突发新闻速度上，远非日报所能企及。当报纸最终开始大规模设置付费墙时，互联网却让人们轻而易举地复制文章内容并在付费墙外传播。整个商业模式彻底崩塌，以至于现在只有极少数大报能够勉强生存。

That scale of copyright dilution and forced unbundling is the worst-case scenario for media businesses in the age of AI. It’s possible arts jobs could survive via consumers’ deep-seated aversion to explicitly AI-generated content, but AI is increasingly being used throughout media in ways invisible to the average end consumer. Roughly 32% of workers in the overall arts, entertainment, and recreation sector use Generative AI to some extent, which is less than the 62% average across all industries, but still enough that virtually every major media project could have some AI within its workflow.

那种规模的版权稀释和强制拆分，是 AI 时代媒体企业的最坏情况。有可能艺术岗位能够依靠消费者对明确 AI 生成内容的深层反感而幸存，但 AI 正越来越多地以普通最终消费者不可见的方式贯穿整个媒体行业使用。总体艺术、娱乐和休闲行业中大约有 32% 的员工以一定程度使用 Generative AI，这低于所有行业 62% 的平均水平，但仍足以使几乎每个重大媒体项目的工作流程中都包含一些 AI。

Indeed, AI is likely seeping into media production processes in ways large companies themselves would struggle to prevent even when they desire to—how can a TV studio be sure nobody in their writers’ room is consulting ChatGPT for jokes or any storyboard artist is generating concept art? And even if professional TV and movie studios do effectively hold out against temptation and prevent internal AI use, how long can they compete with the large mass of wannabe independent creators with much fewer scruples? Plenty of media businesses tried to hold out against the algorithmic content waves of the 2010s and were buried as a result.

事实上，AI 很可能正以一种连大公司都难以阻止的方式渗透到媒体制作流程中。即使大公司希望阻止，也无法做到——一个电视工作室如何能确保其编剧室里没有人使用 ChatGPT 来搜集笑话，或者 storyboard 艺术家没有使用 AI 生成概念艺术？即使专业的电视和电影工作室确实抵制住了诱惑并防止了内部使用 AI，他们又能与大量良心更低的独立创作者竞争多久？许多媒体企业曾试图抵制 2010 年代的算法内容浪潮，结果却被淘汰。

Conclusions

结论

Yet fundamentally, it’s difficult to meaningfully predict how new technologies will interact with existing arts businesses. Take the unexpected resurgence in book sales over the last four years. The novel as a commercial art form had been struggling for decades, with fewer books sold in 2019 than at the beginning of the millennium, but the last six years have seen an unprecedented 70% surge in sales. The unlikely savior of the printed word came from perhaps its polar opposite—TikTok.

然而，从根本上说，很难有意义地预测新技术将如何与现有的艺术业务相互作用。以过去四年书籍销售的意外反弹为例。小说作为一种商业艺术形式已经挣扎了几十年，2019年比新千年初的销量更少，但过去六年出现了前所未有的70%的销量增长。印刷文字的意外救星或许来自其对立面——TikTok。

Of course, fewer people read now than ever before—for the general public, short-form video apps have accelerated the displacement of reading, just as TV, video games, or social media before them. Yet for a dwindling number of dedicated repeat readers, “BookTok” became a new way to source reviews, analysis, discourse, and community in a way that boosted the reading experience and absolutely turbocharged book sales. It’s possible that AI tools could have those same totally unpredictable spillovers for other museums, concerts, or other forms of art in ways that are unpredictable today, in much the same way short-form video saved books in ways that could never have been anticipated beforehand.

当然，现在阅读的人比以往任何时候都要少——对普通大众而言，短视频应用程序加速了阅读的取代，正如电视、视频游戏或社交媒体之前那样。然而，对于逐渐减少的少数忠实重复读者来说，“BookTok”成为了一个全新的方式来获取评论、分析、讨论和社区，从而提升了阅读体验并绝对地推动了图书销售。有可能的是，AI 工具可能在博物馆、音乐会或其他艺术形式中产生出同样不可预料的溢出效应，与短视频意外拯救书籍的方式非常相似，这些效果在此之前是绝对无法预料的。

At the end of the day, the arts are only a small sector of the overall macroeconomy. Media made up a small share of the labor market even at its peak, and it has always been difficult to get hired in creative industries to the point that making fun of art students’ job prospects became an easy punchline. The movie industry has an income profile closer to eggs or bicycles than something major like healthcare or finance. Were the goal to create art for art’s sake, for the intangible and nonmonetizable cultural benefits, it would be relatively easy to counterbalance any economic impacts of AI on artists just by reversing recent cuts to the National Endowments for the Arts & Humanities.

归根结底，艺术仅占整体宏观经济的一小部分。即使在巅峰时期，媒体行业在劳动力市场中的占比也很小，且向来难以在创意产业获得受聘机会，以至于嘲笑艺术专业学生的就业前景成了现成的笑料。电影行业的收入结构更接近鸡蛋或自行车等行业，而非医疗或金融等支柱产业。若创作艺术的目标纯粹是为艺术而艺术，为了那些无形且不可货币化的文化效益，那么要抵消 AI 对艺术家造成的经济冲击，只需扭转近期对国家艺术与人文基金会预算的削减即可，这相对容易实现。

It’s telling that Anthropic, the most prominent AI lab, has basically never bothered with image, video, or music generation, because the prospective economic benefits are marginal when compared to using AI to tackle math or scientific problems. OpenAI learned this lesson the hard way when it was forced to abandon its video generation platform Sora, deciding it had better use for its limited compute than making synthetic TikToks. Nowadays, the art generation is done primarily by secondary players running smaller models, though even these are large enough to threaten significant disruption to legacy media businesses.

很值得注意的是，Anthropic 这个最具影响力的 AI 实验室基本上从未涉及过图像、视频或音乐生成，因为与使用 AI 解决数学或科学问题相比，潜在的经济利益微乎其微。 OpenAI 艰苦地学习了这一课，当时它被迫放弃了自己的视频生成平台 Sora，决定将有限的 compute 用于更有价值的事情，而不是制作合成 TikToks。 如今，艺术生成主要由运行较小模型的次级玩家来完成，尽管即使这些模型也足够强大，可能对传统媒体业务造成重大冲击。

In other words, the primary impacts of AI art will be on culture and society rather than the macroeconomy. Yet arts jobs might be a microcosm for other “creative-adjacent” work that occupies a much larger share of economic activity. Take the tech sector itself, which is the clearest place where AI-driven job loss has shown up outside the media business, as powerful coding agents replace human programmers. Annual tech job gains stood at nearly 300k in 2022, but the sector has been bleeding jobs every year since then in what is now its longest labor market downturn.

换言之，AI 艺术对文化和社会的影响将是主要影响，而非宏观经济。然而，艺术工作可能成为其他“创造相邻”工作的一个微观缩影，而这些工作占据了经济活动中远大的比重。以科技行业本身为例，它是 AI 驱动就业损失在媒体商业之外最明显的领域，因为强大的编码智能体正在取代人类程序员。2022 年，该行业的年度科技工作增长几乎为 30 万，但自那时以来，该行业每年都在裁减工作岗位，如今已进入其历史最长劳动力市场低迷期。

Right now, AI-driven job displacement has been relatively minor outside of these few narrow sectors. Unemployment is higher than it was four years ago but still below even the 2010s average, and overall job turnover rates remain extremely low. Some white-collar sectors that looked prime for AI automation have even been on a hiring spree over the last few years, including legal and engineering firms. Yet if the economic impact of AI ends up being anywhere near large enough to validate the trillions of dollars investors are currently betting on it, these economic disruptions will only spread from here.

目前，AI 驱动的岗位替代在现正相对平缓，仅限于这些少数几个狭窄的行业。失业率高于四年前，但仍低于2010年代平均水平，整体而言岗位流动率极低。一些原本被视为适合AI自动化的白领行业，在过去几年甚至处于招聘热潮，其中包括[法律]和[工程]公司。然而，如果AI的经济影响最终达到足以验证投资者[trillions of dollars investors are currently betting on it]的程度，这些经济冲击将只会从此蔓延。

from: The Goose Programming Language

A memory-safe systems language with no heap allocator, garbage collector, or lifetime annotations. In this repository’s benchmarks, Goose runs faster than C++ and Rust while using less memory.

这是一种内存安全的系统级编程语言，它摒弃了堆分配器、垃圾回收器和生命周期注解。在本仓库的基准测试中，Goose 的运行速度超过了 C++ 和 Rust，同时内存占用更低。

Tutorial · Reference · Specification · Packages · Samples · Benchmarks · Standard library

教程 · 参考 · 规范 · 包 · 示例 · 基准测试 · 标准库

Goose has syntax familiar to C and Rust programmers, but there is no heap. Every dynamic value lives inline on data stacks managed by the compiler. Growth advances a pointer, and memory is freed when its scope ends. The language’s type and lifetime rules make this memory model safe to use.

Goose 的语法对 C 和 Rust 程序员来说很熟悉，但没有堆。每个动态值都内联在由编译器管理的数据栈上。栈的增长只需移动指针，当作用域结束时，内存即被释放。该语言的类型和生命周期规则使得这种内存模型可以安全使用。

Why Goose

为什么选择 Goose

  • Faster than C++ and than safe Rust, while memory safe. Over sixteen benchmarks Goose runs at 3.3x the speed of idiomatic C++, 1.16x hand-optimized C++ and 1.12x the best safe Rust, and uses 1.9x, 1.3x and 1.2x less memory (results). These gains come from Goose’s data layouts and memory model.
  • No allocator, no GC, no reference counting, no destructors. Memory is a handful of data stacks that the compiler assigns statically. Freeing a structure with a million elements takes a single store, no matter how deeply it is nested.
  • Growth preserves references. A reference into a growing array stays valid for as long as the array does. In the corresponding benchmarks, Goose keeps typed references where C++ must call reserve and safe Rust uses u32 indices.
  • Memory safe with zero annotations. There is no lifetime syntax, there are no aliasing or exclusivity rules, and there is no unsafe. The compiler infers what every reference is rooted at and rejects references that could outlive their owners.
  • Nested data stays inline. A string, an array of strings, a record with variable-size fields and an array of those records are each stored as one contiguous block that contains no pointers. A example record that takes 160 bytes and one allocation in C++ takes 29 bytes and no allocations in Goose.
  • Variable sized Enums. Variable-mode ADTs store each value at the size of its own variant rather than that of the largest variant. On the benchmark that exercises this, they use 4x less memory than a Rust enum and run at 2x its speed.
  • Links narrower than pointers. A relative reference stores a typed, checked link as a 1, 2 or 4-byte offset. Structures built from them are position independent, so a data structure can be written to a file as is. Saving it is a single write, and loading it is a single read followed by a verification pass that rejects malformed or hostile data.
  • Everything is built in place, guaranteed. A value is constructed at its final destination through any depth of calls. items.push(parse(line)) writes the parsed record directly into the array, and returning a growable array by value does not copy it.

One memory model: data stacks freed at scope exit

一个 memory model: data stacks freed at scope exit

A program has the native call stack, static data and N data stacks, where the compiler works out N. A data stack is a large address-space reservation with a bump pointer, and there is no other memory. At most one resizable value is live per stack and it is always on top, so growth never moves anything and never checks a capacity. All of this is proved at compile time; the runtime tracks only the bump pointers.

该程序具有本地调用栈、静态数据和 N 个数据栈，其中 N 由编译器自动计算。数据栈是一块大型地址空间预留区域，配备一个 bump pointer，程序中不使用其他内存。每个栈上最多有一个可调整大小的值处于活跃状态，且该值始终位于栈顶，因此栈的增长既不会移动任何数据，也不需要检查容量限制。所有这些特性都是在编译时静态证明的；运行时仅需跟踪 bump pointer。

    for i in 100000 { scratch.push((i % 256) as! u8); }
    print("round ", round, ": ", scratch.len, " bytes");
}                                                     // the free: one store to the stack top

A reference must not outlive the variable that owns its target or access that target through an incompatible type. The compiler infers roots and specializes functions for them, so no annotations are needed. There are no aliasing or exclusivity rules. Links narrower than pointers

比指针更窄的链接

A T& is a machine address: it takes eight bytes and never dangles. A relative reference is the same link stored as a narrow offset. A T&<u32> is measured from the field itself to a target in the same array, so the structure is position independent. A T&<u32 in pool> is measured from the base of a named pool, so other arrays can link into the pool. T&<u32>? uses offset 0 as null. Here is a binary search tree in one grow-only array, with 12-byte nodes:

T& 是一个机器地址，占用八个字节，且永远不会为空。相对引用 则是以窄偏移形式存储同一链接的方式。T&<u32> 的测量是从字段本身到同一数组中目标位置的距离，因此结构是位置独立的。T&<u32 in pool> 的测量是从命名池的基底开始，因此其他数组可以链接到池中。T&<u32>? 使用偏移量 0 作为空值表示。以下是一个包含 12 字节节点的、一维数组中的二叉搜索树：

struct Node { key: i32, left: Node&<u32>?, right: Node&<u32>? }   // 12 bytes, links included

> fn insert(pool: Node[>..]&, key: i32) {
>     if pool.len == 0 { pool.push(Node { key: key }); return; }
>     var cur .= pool[0];                             // .= binds a reference; = would copy the node
>     loop {
>         if key == cur.key { return; }
>         let next = if key < cur.key { cur.left } else { cur.right };
>         if next { cur .= next; continue; }          // narrowed by `if`: next is a Node&
>         if key < cur.key { cur.left .= pool.push(Node { key: key }); }
>         else             { cur.right .= pool.push(Node { key: key }); }
>         return;
>     }
> }
> ```

```rust
fn insert(pool: Node[>..]&, key: i32) {
    if pool.len == 0 { pool.push(Node { key: key }); return; }
    var cur .= pool[0];                             // .= 绑定了一个引用；= 会复制节点
    loop {
        if key == cur.key { return; }
        let next = if key < cur.key { cur.left } else { cur.right };
        if next { cur .= next; continue; }          // 由 `if` 收窄：next 是 Node&
        if key < cur.key { cur.left .= pool.push(Node { key: key }); }
        else             { cur.right .= pool.push(Node { key: key }); }
        return;
    }
}

References are transparent (there is no * or ->). .= binds or retargets a reference, and Node? is a nullable reference that if, guard and assert narrow. The insert is one push and one store, and the push cannot invalidate cur. When lifetimes are not nested, a reusable pool pairs a grow-only array with a hidden freelist. alloc_ref reuses a free slot or pushes a new one, and free returns a slot to the pool. Since a slot’s memory is never actually freed, a stale slot reads a different value of the correct type rather than corrupting memory.

引用是透明的（没有 * 或 ->）。.= 绑定或重定向引用，而 Node? 是一个可空引用，可被 if、guard 和 assert 收窄。插入操作包含一次 push 和一次 store，且 push 不会使 cur 失效。当生命周期不嵌套时，reusable 池将只增长数组与隐藏的 freelist 配对。alloc_ref 重用一个空闲槽位或推入一个新的槽位，而 free 将槽位返回给池。由于槽位的内存实际上从未被释放，过期槽位读取的是正确类型的另一个值，而不是破坏内存。

Saving and loading data as bytes

以字节形式保存和加载数据

var loaded, ok = from_bytes<Node[>..]>(image);  // verified before it becomes a value
image[image.len - 3] = 200;                     // tamper with a link ...
var bad, bok = from_bytes<Node[>..]>(image);    // ... and it is false and an empty array

The tree’s links are self-relative, so the tree means the same thing wherever it is stored. Saving it writes its bytes and loading it reads them back, with no serializer, no schema and no pointer fixups. from_bytes checks the framing, every tag, every length and every link before the bytes become a value, so a corrupt or hostile file makes it return false, never a wild reference.

该树的链接是自相对的，因此无论存储在何处，该树的含义均保持不变。保存操作直接写入其字节，加载操作直接读回字节，无需序列化器、无需模式定义，也无需指针修正。from_bytes 在字节变为值之前，会校验帧结构、每个标签、每个长度和每个链接，因此损坏或恶意构造的文件会导致其返回 false，而绝不会产生野指针。

In-place construction

原地构造

The copy-free construction guarantee (spec §4.3) says a constructed value is always built at its final location, which is passed down through calls. A function returning a grow-only array by value writes its elements directly into the caller’s variable, or into a field of the record being built inside another array, so out-parameters are rarely needed.

无拷贝构造保证（spec §4.3）指出，构造出的值总是在其最终位置构建，该位置通过调用传递下去。一个按值返回只增长数组的函数，会将其元素直接写入调用者的变量，或者写入正在另一个数组内部构建的记录的字段中，因此几乎不需要输出参数。

跨调用返回错误

fn parse_user(line: u8[:]) -> User {              // 返回一个 User：无 Result，无错误参数

return E from f returns E as the result of the innermost active call of f, however many frames up that call is. Every function in between keeps its plain signature. The construct is checked statically: every call of parse_user must lie inside a load call, so nothing can go uncaught at runtime. # 编译为 C 及调用 C

## Introduction

当我们讨论将高级语言编译为 C 时，可以想象我们正在构建一个**抽象机器**（Abstract Machine）。这个抽象机器定义了我们希望实现的计算行为，而具体的实现细节则交由编译器来决定。

## Why compile to C?

将高级语言编译为 C 有几个显著优势：

1. **移植性**：C 有一个广泛的跨平台实现，几乎可以在所有主流操作系统上运行，这使得我们生成的代码能够无缝移植。

2. **成熟生态**：C 拥有世界级的编译器（如 GCC、Clang）和静态链接器，这些工具经过多年发展，性能和可靠性都得到了保障。

3. **优化栈**：C 编译器通常包含 sophisticated 的优化器，这些优化可以显著提升我们生成代码的性能。

4. **Interoperability with C Libraries**：大量现有的 C 库可以直接链接，我们无需额外包装即可利用这些资源。

5. **调试支持**：C 调试器（如 GDB）成熟可靠，这为我们调试生成的本机代码提供了便利。

例如，Lua 语言就是将其实现编译为 C，然后通过编写 Lua C 绑定来进行调用。Rust 语言的 `cc` 包也采用类似策略。

如果我们想进一步深入，可以考虑 **WebAssembly**（WebAssembly），它提供了更现代的跨平台目标。

## How do we compile to C?

编译器的基本策略相当直接。我们首先生成一个**抽象语法树**（AST），然后通过遍历 AST 来生成 C 代码。对于每一种需要转换的抽象机器指令，我们都有一个对应的 C 生成函数。

假设我们的抽象机器支持以下指令：

- `push_const <const_id>`：将常量压入栈
- `push_arg <arg_id>`：将参数压入栈
- `call_native <fn_name>`：调用原生函数

对应的 C 生成函数可能如下：

```c
void gen_push_const(int const_id) {
    printf("  __push_const(%d);\n", const_id);
}

void gen_push_arg(int arg_id) {
    printf("  __push_arg(%d);\n", arg_id);
}

void gen_call_native(const char* fn_name) {
    printf("  __call_native(\"%s\");\n", fn_name);
}

这些函数接收 AST 中的指令对象，不需要返回值，而是直接输出对应的 C 代码到标准输出。

The call interface

为了在 C 程序中调用我们生成的抽象机器，必须为其提供一个标准接口。这个接口包含：

  1. 初始化：设置必要的运行时状态和栈空间
  2. 字节码载入：将编译后的字节码加载到内存中
  3. 执行控制：启动抽象机器的运行
  4. 清理：释放占用的资源

假设我们的抽象机器被命名为 抽象机器，那么其 C 接口可能如下：

// 初始化抽象机器
void machine_init(abстракт_machine* m);

// 加载字节码
void machine_load_bytecode(abстракт_machine* m, const uint8_t* code, size_t code_size);

// 执行字节码
void machine_run(abстракт_machine* m);

// 清理资源
void machine_cleanup(abстракт_machine* m);

Where the speed comes from

速度从何而来

Much of the speed comes from the memory model: no heap allocation or per-object teardown, contiguous data, narrow links, and enums sized for the variant they contain. Every index is bounds-checked, and the compiler removes checks it can prove unnecessary. An assert on a slice length often lets the compiler remove the remaining checks in a kernel, so that the kernel can be vectorized. --bce-lines reports the checks that remain. checkfree fn rejects a kernel if any bounds check remains in it; index types let graph edges keep the validation done while the graph was built. Benchmark measurements use whole-process wall-clock time, including teardown.

Limitations

限制

  • You have to think about where data lives: who owns it, and how long its scope lasts. Usually the owner is the function that builds the data, which needs no extra work; when it is not, the data goes in a reusable pool.
  • Recursive functions cannot keep growable data across a recursive call. Scratch data must end before the call, and data that outlives the call is passed in as a pool.
  • Arrays of variable-size elements can be iterated but not indexed (unless you keep an index of references beside them). A fixed-mode enum cannot be pointed into, and a variable-mode one cannot be overwritten. You make this choice per container.
  • There are no escaping closures, no function pointers and no dynamic dispatch beyond ADT tags, and only whole-program compilation is supported.
  • A slot that was returned to a reusable pool but is still referenced reads whatever its next owner put there. That is a logic bug, but never memory corruption.
  • 你必须考虑数据存储的位置：谁拥有它，以及其作用域持续多久。通常，拥有者是构建数据的函数，这无需额外工作；如果不是，数据将进入 reusable 池。
  • 递归函数不能在递归调用之间保留可增长的数据。临时数据必须在调用前结束，而超出调用生命周期的数据会作为池传入。
  • 可变大小元素的数组可以迭代但不能索引（除非在旁边保留一份引用索引）。固定模式的枚举不能被指向，而可变模式的枚举不能被覆写。你需要针对每个容器做出这种选择。
  • 不支持逃逸闭包、函数指针，以及超出 ADT 标签的动态分派，且仅支持全程序编译。
  • 返回到 reusable 池但仍被引用的槽位，会读取其下一个所有者放入的任何内容。这是一个逻辑错误，但绝不会导致内存损坏。

--debug 标志会开启生成的 C 代码中的溢出、范围和标签检查，并使用调试信息来构建 C 代码。当这些检查导致中止时，会打印出源代码行号（对于溢出或类型转换，还会打印相关值）。--dry-run 标志可以打印构建过程中会执行的命令，方便用户在自己的构建系统中使用。-v 标志则会打印命令在运行时的输出。中间文件存储在 ~/.goose（即 GOOSE_HOME）目录下，其中运行时对象会根据 C 编译器的不同重新编译一次。适用于运行和构建两种模式的常用标志包括：-O0/-O1/-O2 用于设置内联级别（默认 -O2）、--bce-lines 用于报告每个保留边界检查的行数，以及 -DGS_DEBUG=1 是 --debug 标志设置的定义。每个可调整大小的值都存储在 2 GB 的保留地址空间的数据栈中，按需分配。--stack-reserve 16G 标志可以更改程序的栈大小。--stacks 标志可以报告程序及其每个工作线程可以使用的栈数量，以及由此产生的 hardware_threads() 限制。-DGS_STACK_STATS=1 标志可以使程序在结束时报告其实际的栈使用情况。

A program with C of its own lists that C in a sidecar file beside the source, foo.build beside foo.goose: c_sources = ["impl.c"];. The sidecar can also set c_include, c_defines and c_libs, and each of these has _windows, _linux or _macos variants for the part that applies to one platform. Both forms build the C: goose build links it in, and goose run builds it into a library that the in-process run loads, so an extern fn can call it either way. A library does the same with a sidecar beside its entry file (or names the static library target of its own CMake project, cmake_target = "x";, which the compiler builds through cmake). A program uses a library by writing import name from "source"; in its root file. The source is a directory ("./lib"), or a git repository at a tag or commit ("owner/repo@v1" on GitHub, "host/owner/repo@ref"), which is fetched into ~/.goose and built there once per C compiler (docs/design/packages.md).

一个拥有自己的 C 代码的程序在源文件旁的 sidecar 文件中列出该 C 代码，即 foo.build 位于 foo.goose 旁边：c_sources = ["impl.c"];。

sidecar 还可以设置 c_include、c_defines 和 c_libs，每个都有 _windows、_linux 或 _macos 变体，用于仅适用于单个平台的部分。

两种形式都会构建 C：goose build 将其链接入程序，而 goose run 将其构建为库，由进程内运行加载，因此 extern fn 可以两种方式调用它。

库也以同样的方式处理，sidecar 位于其入口文件旁边（或者命名其自身 CMake 项目的静态库目标，cmake_target = "x";，编译器通过 cmake 构建它）。

程序在其根文件中编写 import name from "source"; 来使用库。

源是一个目录（"./lib"），或者一个位于标签或提交处的 git 仓库（GitHub 上的 "owner/repo@v1"，"host/owner/repo@ref"），它会被获取到 ~/.goose 中，并按每个 C 编译器构建一次（docs/design/packages.md）。

Underneath, goose -o tour.c tour.goose writes the C. That file holds the program and the part of the runtime that is inlined into it. The rest of the runtime (the OS layer, data stack reservation, threads, printing) is one more C file, which goose --emit-runtime goose_runtime.c writes. It is compiled once and linked with every program (cc -O2 tour.c goose_runtime.o -o tour -lm -pthread; on Windows cl /O2 tour.c goose_runtime.obj). Build the runtime with the same C compiler and flags the programs use. It takes no -D of its own, and a program from another version of the compiler fails to link against it. --standalone instead writes a C file that holds the whole runtime, and that file builds on its own. A program using audio, gfx, physics or ui also links that module’s layer. goose --audio-link msvc|cc, --gfx-link, --physics-link and --ui-link print a response file that names the layer (cc cube.c goose_runtime.o -o cube @$(goose --gfx-link cc); a ui program puts the ui layer before the gfx layer it draws through). goose build --dry-run prints all of this for the program at hand.

在下面的代码中，goose -o tour.c tour.goose 生成了 C 语言文件。该文件包含程序以及被内联到其中的运行时的一部分。剩余的运行时（包括操作系统层、数据栈保留、线程和打印等）被生成为另一个 C 文件，使用 goose --emit-runtime goose_runtime.c 实现。它只被编译一次，然后与每个程序链接（命令为 cc -O2 tour.c goose_runtime.o -o tour -lm -pthread，Windows 系统上为 cl /O2 tour.c goose_runtime.obj）。构建运行时时，请使用与程序相同的 C 编译器和标志。它不接受额外的 -D 参数，如果使用其他版本的编译器生成的程序将无法与其链接。--standalone 选项则生成一个包含整个运行时的 C 文件，该文件可以独立编译。如果程序使用了 audio、gfx、physics 或 ui 等模块，还需要链接相应的模块层。使用 goose --audio-link msvc|cc、--gfx-link、--physics-link 和 --ui-link 等命令，可以生成一个响应文件，其中列出了对应的层（例如，cc cube.c goose_runtime.o -o cube @$(goose --gfx-link cc)；ui 程序会将 ui 层放在它所绘制的 gfx 层之前）。goose build --dry-run 命令可以打印当前程序的所有这些信息。

状态

Goose is new. What exists today is a whole-program compiler of about thirty thousand lines of C++, the specification, the standard library, the samples, and a test suite that CI runs on Windows, macOS and Linux with an extra sanitizer job. These are deliberately out of scope for now: moves for resizable values, more than one resizable per struct, labeled break, namespace privacy, and more OS/library access. Open items are tracked in the specification’s Appendix B.

History & Use of AI

AI 历史 与 用途

This repo was produced almost entirely with AI, from a human language design. I had designed Goose several years ago, and had started to implement it, but running a game startup (which is built on another programming language of mine, Lobster) there was no time to finish it. Which was sad, because I knew Goose could do things other languages can’t, and it should exist.

本仓库几乎完全由 AI 生成，源于一个人类设计的语言。

我几年前设计了 Goose，并开始实现它，但由于在运营一家游戏初创公司（该公司基于我设计的另一门编程语言 Lobster），没有时间完成它。

这很遗憾，因为我知道 Goose 能做其他语言做不到的事情，它应该存在。

I had not expected AI to help with this until Fable came out. I thought it might be capable enough to do a good job. I made it essentially clone the style and structure of my other recent compiler (Lobster), which is why if you look at the code, it looks rather similar to that. My initial design had left lots of things unspecified, and lots of back and forth with Fable made me decide on all of those, and it is now a better language for it.

我本不指望 AI 能在这方面提供帮助，直到 Fable 问世。我认为它可能有足够的能力胜任这项工作。我让它基本上克隆了我另一款近期编译器（Lobster）的风格和结构，这就是为什么如果你看代码，会发现它看起来与那款编译器相当相似。我最初的设计留下了许多未明确规定的细节，而与 Fable 反复多次交流后，让我最终敲定了所有这些细节，这也使其成为了一门更优秀的语言。

It is also an experiment in using AI to implement a new language, rather than reproduce an existing one.

这也是一个实验，探索利用 AI 来实现一种新语言，而非复现已有语言。

You may wonder why I had it work in C++, if clearly I could have used any language, like Rust, or my own Lobster, or.. Goose itself (that may still happen). With Fable, it was my observation that it is almost equally capable in any language, and the strong guardrails of Rust or other languages are not as pressing as they once were. Since the compiler emits C, you likely already need to have a C/C++ compiler around, so sticking inside one ecosystem would seem to simplify deployment and adoption. I’ve also integrated libtcc and who knows what other C libraries in the future. And, like I said, to have the compiler code mimic my existing Lobster compiler seemed fun, at least I can read it like it is my own.

你可能会好奇我为什么让它在 C++ 中工作，如果很明显我本可以使用任何语言，比如 Rust，或者我自己的 Lobster，或者……Goose 本身（那可能还是会发生）。就 Fable 而言，我观察到它在任何语言中的能力几乎都差不多，而且 Rust 或其他语言的强约束机制不再像过去那样紧迫。既然编译器生成 C 代码，你很可能已经需要有一个 C/C++ 编译器在手边，所以在一个生态系统内工作似乎会简化部署和采用。我还集成了 libtcc，未来谁知道还会集成哪些其他 C 库。而且，正如我所说，让编译器代码模仿我现有的 Lobster 编译器似乎很有趣，至少我可以像阅读自己的代码一样阅读它。
